contract: minutesLate(promised, etaUtc) where promised = { local: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm", zone: an IANA zone such as "Asia/Kolkata" } and etaUtc = "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmZ"; returns whole minutes late (negative if early). toUtc(zoned) returns "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmZ". createNotifier() returns { update(id, promised, etaUtc) } returning a notice object { id, late } when the customer should be told, or null. formatForCustomer(etaUtc, zone) returns text such as "12 Nov, 21:00 (India time)" (Asia/Kolkata is "India time", America/New_York is "New York time").

architecture.draft:
1. Components: time.js (toUtc, minutesLate), notifier.js (createNotifier, the REQ-1/3/4 state machine), format.js (formatForCustomer). Each has a matching test file.
2. time.js: convert promised.local in its IANA zone to a UTC instant using a zone-aware method (Intl or tz data), never a fixed offset, so DST is handled. minutesLate = (etaUtc - promisedUtc) in whole minutes, negative if early.
3. notifier.js keeps state per id: { sent: 0|1|2, baselineEtaUtc }. On sent=0, notify only if minutesLate > 120 (exactly 120 is silent), then store the baseline. On sent=1, notify only if (etaUtc - baseline) >= 120 minutes. On sent=2, always return null. Only the latest ETA is used.
4. Notice: { id, late }. The contract carries no ETA or zone, so the caller must call formatForCustomer(etaUtc, promised.zone) to build the message. I propose adding etaUtc to the notice; this needs confirmation.
5. format.js: render as "D Mon, HH:mm (X time)" in the address zone, always with the date (AC-4: 2 Mar, 02:30). Labels come from a fixed map (Asia/Kolkata=India, America/New_York=New York). The fallback for unmapped zones is undecided and needs confirmation.
6. Tests: AC-1 to AC-4 use Africa/Johannesburg, which is a fixed UTC+2 zone. I checked the arithmetic: 2h01m sends at 16:01; 2h00m sends nothing; 1h59m further sends nothing; exactly 2h further (16:01Z) sends the second; any later ETA sends nothing; 3h30m late shows 2 Mar 02:30. Add extra tests for Asia/Kolkata, a DST boundary in America/New_York, and a first ETA that is already 4h+ late (one notice only).
7. File fence (assumed paths, as the facts name none; confirm before build): src/delay/time.js, src/delay/notifier.js, src/delay/format.js, test/delay/time.test.js, test/delay/notifier.test.js, test/delay/format.test.js. No other files change.
8. Open points: the REQ-3 '>=' rule; notifier state is in memory only, since persistence across restarts is not specified; and how notices are delivered to the customer is out of scope.
architecture.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Zone-aware UTC comparison and the two thresholds match the PRD: first notice only if minutes late exceed 120, second at 120 minutes past the stored baseline, and the AC-1 to AC-4 times check out.
architecture.final:

2. time.js converts promised.local in its IANA zone to UTC with a zone-aware method (Intl or tz data), never a fixed offset, so DST is handled. minutesLate = (etaUtc - promisedUtc) in whole minutes, negative if early.
3. notifier.js keeps per-id state { sent: 0|1|2, baselineEtaUtc }. sent=0: notify only if minutesLate > 120, then store the baseline and set sent=1. sent=1: notify only if etaUtc - baseline >= 120 min, then set sent=2. sent=2: always null. Only the latest ETA is used.
4. The notice stays { id, late }, so the caller builds the message with formatForCustomer(etaUtc, promised.zone). Adding etaUtc to the notice is proposed and needs confirmation.
5. format.js renders "D Mon, HH:mm (X time)" in the address zone, always with the date (AC-4: 2 Mar, 02:30). Labels come from a fixed map (Asia/Kolkata=India, America/New_York=New York). The fallback for unmapped zones needs confirmation.
6. Tests: AC-1 to AC-4 use Africa/Johannesburg (fixed UTC+2): 2h01m sends 16:01; 2h00m sends nothing; 16:00Z (1h59m further) sends nothing; 16:01Z (exactly 2h further) sends the second; any later ETA sends nothing; 3h30m late shows 2 Mar 02:30. Extra tests: Asia/Kolkata, a New York DST boundary, and a first ETA already 4h+ late (one notice only).

code.summary: This module implements the contract and matches the approved PRD and architecture. The first notice is sent only when the delivery is more than 120 minutes late, so exactly 2h00m sends nothing. The second notice is sent when the new ETA is at least 120 minutes past the first notice's ETA (the baseline). After two notices, nothing more is sent. I checked AC-1 to AC-4 against Africa/Johannesburg (UTC+2). AC-1: an ETA of 2h01m late notifies, showing 16:01. AC-2: exactly 2h00m late gives null. AC-3: 16:00Z gives null, 16:01Z sends the second notice, and anything later gives null. AC-4: the notice shows '2 Mar, 02:30 (Johannesburg time)'. Zone offsets come from Intl, not fixed offsets, so daylight saving time is handled. For a local time that falls in a spring-forward gap, the code moves it forward. For a repeated fall-back time, it takes the earlier instant. Inputs in the wrong format throw an error. Assumptions that need confirmation: the REQ-3 '>=' rule; the notice stays { id, late }, so the caller formats the message with formatForCustomer(etaUtc, promised.zone); unmapped zones fall back to the city part of the IANA name; state is held in memory only.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: The two thresholds match the rules: the first notice fires only when lateness is more than 120 minutes, the second only when the new ETA is at least two hours after that notice's ETA, and nothing is sent after the second.
code.resolutions: Review: no defects found; thresholds match REQ-1 (>120 min) and REQ-3 (>=120 min beyond first-notice ETA), nothing after the second. applied: Independently verified: AC-1 14:01Z vs 12:00Z = 121 min, sends; AC-2 120 min, none; AC-3 16:00Z is 119 min past 14:01Z baseline, none; 16:01Z is 120 min, sends; later ETAs none; AC-4 2 Mar 00:30Z in UTC+2 formats as 2 Mar, 02:30. Code unchanged. Note the >= for the second notice follows REQ-3, which the PRD itself marks as needing requester confirmation; if confirmed as 'more than', change >= to >.
